steps: Given: m = 1000 kg, a = 4 m s⁻², S = 50 m, t = 5 s
Required: Power, P
Force: F = ma
Substitution: F = 1000 kg × 4 m s⁻² = 4000 N
Work: W = FS
Substitution: W = 4000 N × 50 m = 2.0 × 10⁵ J
Power: P = W/t
Substitution: P = (2.0 × 10⁵ J)/(5 s)
Working: P = 4.0 × 10⁴ W = 40 kW
Work is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force: W = Fs.
When the object remains at rest, its displacement is zero.
Therefore, the work done is zero.
items.finalAnswer: The work done is zero because the object's displacement is zero.

steps: Kinetic energy depends on both the mass and the speed of an object: K.E. = ½mv².
A car has much greater mass than a motorcycle.
Therefore, even at a lower speed, the car may have more kinetic energy than the motorcycle.
items.finalAnswer: The car's much greater mass can give it more kinetic energy, even if it moves more slowly.

steps: Given: W₁ = 5 J, t₁ = 10 s; W₂ = 3 J, t₂ = 5 s
Required: Which force delivers greater power
Formula: P = W/t
Substitution: P₁ = 5 J/10 s = 0.5 W
Substitution: P₂ = 3 J/5 s = 0.6 W
Working: 0.6 W > 0.5 W
Therefore, force F₂ delivers greater power.
Gravitational potential energy is given by P.E. = mgh.
The woman runs up the same stairs, so her mass and the height gained remain unchanged.
The speed does not affect the gain in gravitational potential energy.
Therefore, her gain in potential energy remains 4500 J.
items.finalAnswer: Her gain in potential energy is 4500 J.

steps: Work is done when a force produces displacement in the direction of the force.
Work is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force: W = Fs.
The SI unit of work is the joule (J).
One joule is the work done when a force of one newton displaces an object one metre in the direction of the force.
items.finalAnswer: Work is force multiplied by displacement in the direction of the force; its SI unit is the joule (J).

steps: The potential energy of a body is the work done in raising it against gravity.
For a body of mass m raised through a vertical height h, P.E. = mgh.
Here, g is the acceleration due to gravity.
items.finalAnswer: The potential energy of a body of mass m raised through height h is P.E. = mgh.

steps: Let a body of mass m be accelerated from rest to velocity v by a force F through displacement s.
The work done on the body is W = Fs.
Using F = ma, W = mas.
From v² = u² + 2as and u = 0, s = v²/(2a).
Substituting for s: W = ma × v²/(2a) = ½mv².
This work is stored in the body as kinetic energy.
Therefore, K.E. = ½mv².
items.finalAnswer: The kinetic energy of a moving body is K.E. = ½mv².
